rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CX Of the Stature, Forme, or shape of the Body
rules.historical_only_meaning: Printed chapter CX (editorial CXI) begins on PDF580 below the divider, after the prior intellect chapter.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: that Planet who doth partilly behold the Lord of the ascendant
rules.historical_only_meaning: Lilly derives alleged tall versus short stature primarily from a planet in a partile aspect to the Lord of Ascendant.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if many doe behold him, then judge from the strongest
rules.historical_only_meaning: When multiple planets aspect the Ascendant ruler, he says to judge stature using the strongest rather than treating all factors equally.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Orientall A moderate stature declining rather to brevity
rules.historical_only_meaning: Oriental Saturn is said to indicate medium height tending toward shorter stature.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Occidentall A short stature
rules.historical_only_meaning: Occidental Saturn is alleged to indicate short stature.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter Orientall A goodly tall stature
rules.historical_only_meaning: Oriental Jupiter is alleged to indicate tall stature.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter Occidentall Of moderate stature but inclining to tallness
rules.historical_only_meaning: Occidental Jupiter is alleged to indicate medium-to-tall stature, not simply short.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Orientall Tall Stature
rules.historical_only_meaning: Oriental Mars is alleged to indicate tall stature.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Occidentall Moderate in height but more long then short
rules.historical_only_meaning: Occidental Mars is alleged to indicate middle height inclining taller than shorter.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus Orientall One more tall and slender
rules.historical_only_meaning: Oriental Venus is alleged to indicate taller and slender build, not height alone.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus Occidentall Of more short stature inclining to brevity
rules.historical_only_meaning: Occidental Venus is alleged to indicate shorter stature.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury Orientall One of middle stature but verging to height
rules.historical_only_meaning: Oriental Mercury is alleged to signify average height trending taller.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury Occidentall Of small stature or but moderately tall
rules.historical_only_meaning: Occidental Mercury is said to indicate smaller or moderately tall stature, a deliberately broad outcome.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury whether he be Orientall or Occidentall ... Dispositor
rules.historical_only_meaning: Lilly explicitly states Mercury's dispositor modifies body/stature irrespective of oriental versus occidental status.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in his owne house
rules.historical_only_meaning: Mercury in its own domicile is treated as a case where the sign determines stature rather than an orientation table alone.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in the Suns house
rules.historical_only_meaning: Mercury in a house of the Sun is treated as a sign-based stature-modification case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in the Moon her house
rules.historical_only_meaning: Mercury in a house of the Moon is separately named as a sign-based stature-modification case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: The same course the Luminaries observe
rules.historical_only_meaning: The Sun and Moon are said to follow an analogous stature-disposition rule, without full quantitative thresholds.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Of the proportion of the Members
rules.historical_only_meaning: A separate subsection considers overall bodily shape rather than height alone.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: the Signe ascending and his Lord
rules.historical_only_meaning: Body form is to be considered from the rising sign and its ruler; this is not identical to the stature-planet tie-breaker.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: the Planet or Planets in the ascendant or affecting it
rules.historical_only_meaning: Lilly includes planets in the first house and planets forming aspects to the ascendant as distinct sources.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: the two Lights viz Sun and Moon
rules.historical_only_meaning: Both solar and lunar placements are separate testimonies in the author's body-proportion method.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: the season of the yeer
rules.historical_only_meaning: The calendar season is listed among alleged modifiers of proportions, and must not be confused with birth-year cohort effects.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: fixed Starres in the ascendant or neer the cusp thereof
rules.historical_only_meaning: Fixed stars near the ascendant cusp are a further original source condition; no numerical orb is supplied here.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXI Nature of the Signes Colour of the Face and Haire
rules.historical_only_meaning: The next numbered printed chapter begins below the original divider in frame PDF581; its sign/colour/appearance rules are NOT extracted in this batch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: This is sufficiently handled in our Introduction or first Part from pag 93 to 99
rules.historical_only_meaning: The following chapter explicitly cross-references Book I pages 93–99; do not count this cross-reference as a validated stature outcome.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Yet briefly ... twelve sign stature categories
rules.historical_only_meaning: The following printed sign-height categories are reserved for the next batch rather than silently pooled with planetary stature in the current chapter.
